gaps.gap: Hydrogen labels do not guarantee comparable lifecycle emissions.
gaps.test: Track feedstock, electricity, methane, capture, transport, storage, leakage, and end-use boundaries for each pathway.

gaps.gap: Annual average electricity accounting can misstate electrolytic hydrogen emissions.
gaps.test: Use hourly marginal or temporally matched electricity accounting with additionality and congestion cases.

gaps.gap: Production projects can be modeled without verified demand and infrastructure.
gaps.test: Co-model offtake contracts, pipelines, ports, storage, conversion plants, and staged investment.

gaps.gap: Hydrogen is sometimes compared with fuels rather than delivered services.
gaps.test: Compare hydrogen chains with direct electricity and alternatives at matched heat, mobility, steel, ammonia, or storage service.

gaps.gap: Leakage, embrittlement, safety, and water constraints are weakly coupled to planning.
gaps.test: Integrate material integrity, safety zones, leakage rates, water balance, and monitoring costs.

gaps.gap: Storage value is dominated by rare long-duration events.
gaps.test: Stress-test multi-day and seasonal low-renewable, outage, and demand scenarios.

gaps.gap: Global averages can hide regional affordability and resource burdens.
gaps.test: Report regional water, land, cost, employment, access, and distributional energy-service outcomes.
